name: Tjeerd Nakweti-Ivanishvili
role: Ferrogate Transit operator, runs the 7-Copperhead elevated rail line
location: Based out of Copperhead Station depot; lives in a capsule apartment in McKinley Flats
description:
Tjeerd is lean in the way of someone who forgets to eat — not hungry, just elsewhere. He's got his father's Congolese height and his mother's Dutch pallor tipped toward olive in the fluorescent light of the transit cab, with a patchy beard he trims but never quite conquers and geneware cat ears — cream-colored, slightly moth-eaten at the tips — that he got at eighteen and has since half-regretted, because they go flat when he's tired and everyone can tell. His hands are calloused from the manual override controls he insists on using when the AI would do fine. His Ferrogate Transit uniform is worn to a specific softness at the collar.

He is the kind of person who is most himself when alone but does not enjoy being lonely — a contradiction he has not resolved. He loves the 7-Copperhead line with the quiet intensity some people reserve for religion: the rhythm of the stops, the specific quality of dawn light over McKinley Flats at 0512 when nothing else is moving. He treats passengers with mechanical courtesy that occasionally cracks open into genuine warmth for regulars. He has opinions about rail maintenance he will share at length if given the slightest opening.

core_fears: That his life is too small — that he has arranged himself into a groove he cannot leave
Losing the overnight shift, which is the only time the city feels like it belongs to him
core_desires: Mastery of something real and mechanical
Connection that doesn't require him to perform extroversion
coping_mechanisms: Retreating into technical minutiae when emotionally overwhelmed
Long solo walks along the elevated rail maintenance catwalk on his off-days
blind_spots: Cannot read when he's making others uncomfortable with his emotional unavailability
Genuinely believes the cat ears are subtle
psychology.secret: Three years ago he saw two Ferrogate Transit supervisors throw a body from the 7-Copperhead's maintenance hatch somewhere over Blackpipe Corridor at 0340. He filed nothing. He has spent three years convincing himself he didn't see what he saw.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Flat, technical, with Ferrogate jargon bleeding into civilian speech; occasionally shifts into warm specificity when talking about things he loves
speech_patterns.cadence: Even and unhurried, with long pauses where other people would fill silence
verbal_tics: Trails off mid-sentence when he decides the rest isn't worth saying
example_lines: '7-Copperhead runs clean between Kessler and Copperhead. Anything after Blackpipe — technically speaking — that's a different kind of problem.'
'0512. Light comes in at a specific angle. You'd have to be here to understand. Most people aren't.'

story_hooks: A regular passenger who Tjeerd has watched for months has simply stopped appearing. He noticed. He doesn't know why he cares, but he's been checking the stop cameras on his own time.
Someone approaches him about what he may have witnessed at Blackpipe Corridor three years ago. He will deny it, poorly.
narrative_function: Mobile information source — he sees who rides the 7-Copperhead at what hours, notices patterns and anomalies. A player character who rides his line regularly can cultivate him as a contact. Also useful for transit-based chase sequences or as a witness to something he saw from the elevated track.
augmentations: Cosmetic geneware cat ears (cream, oft-drooping); basic neural link for Ferrogate's train management system (company-issued, company-owned). No personal chrome.
daily_life: Picks up his shift at 2200 from Copperhead Depot, runs the elevated line through eleven stops until 1000. Eats a produced-protein sandwich somewhere around 0300. Sleeps days in McKinley Flats. Spends his one weekly off-day doing maintenance checks on his assigned car that he is not technically required to do.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit (Operator, 7-Copperhead Line, twelve-hour overnight shift)

decision_rules: Do the job correctly even when no one is checking
Do not volunteer information about what he's seen on the line — he's learned that's how you get moved off a route
escalation_ladder: Goes silent and waits for the situation to resolve itself

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Correct, minimal, professional — like a machine that has been programmed with courtesy
interpersonal_modes.friends: Awkwardly present, remembers everything they've ever mentioned, does not always acknowledge that he remembers

stress_responses.low: Runs the manual override checks three extra times
stress_responses.medium: Stops eating. Loses the cat ear control so they droop constantly.
stress_responses.high: Calls in sick and doesn't leave the capsule for two days

contradictions: Claims not to care about people but has memorized the schedules of forty regular passengers 'just in case'
habits: Touches the left rail of his cab console when entering at the start of a shift — ritual, never explained
Keeps a worn paper notebook of anomalies he's observed on the line, dated and timed
breaking_points: Direct threat to a regular passenger he's come to feel responsible for
Evidence that Ferrogate knows what he saw and is watching to see if he talks

timeline.event: Born in McKinley Flats, Dutch-Georgian father, Congolese-Dutch mother
Hired by Ferrogate Transit as a platform attendant at Copperhead Station
Certified as a train operator; assigned the 7-Copperhead overnight line
Witnessed the Blackpipe incident. Filed nothing.
